acceptance.output_evidence:
RECORDED, NO VERDICT. Material for the grader.

METHOD: 176,062 exclusions by 17 ordered rules. Rules 1-13 are file-level (test, fixture-named json/yaml, vendored, log, prose, patch, snapshot, record tree, generated, deploy changelog, captured AWS API listing, table, plain text). Rules 14-17 are line-level on code and config files (docstring 1,459; comment 1,136; identifier 1,329; float infinity 23), read with Python tokenize/ast and a small quote-and-comment lexer for js, hcl, sh and yaml. Each rule's count is printed, and the counts sum to the excluded.

JUDGMENT POINTS a grader may weigh:
(1) Record trees are excluded as whole files. That covers 42,287 hits in non-code files under deliverables/, seat folders, audit, threads, ledgers, briefs, runs and research. Code files under those trees were NOT excluded; they are classified by line, so this round's own check_en.py FOUR_BUCKETS shows up as a carrier.
(2) 'generated' is claimed only on evidence the reason quotes: a writer line, an out/ dir, a lockfile, or a header marker naming a tool. Two files with a generated_by naming a seat or worker were kept as carriers (MDPF_PIPELINE_TRUTH.json, PATH_MANIFEST.json). So was NFRA_GRAPHUNI.P1-D.gold_compute_producer.json, whose only marker is 'generated_at': null.
(3) .txt (747) is excluded as 'plain text, not a code or config file type', not as prose. Several are key lists or plan captures.
(4) The fixture-name rule (302) covers aws-shapes/*-hand-audit-fixture-*.yaml and the CVO's fixture json.
(5) The deploy CHANGELOG.json files (3,650) are logs by their own _description.
(6) The ontology instruments/ json (1,128) are captured AWS API listings by content shape.
(7) 73,782 .log/.jsonl hits are the largest class.
